newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian minister confirms Busang deadline.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian minister confirms Busang deadline.

text.p: Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana has said Indonesia will seek investors in the huge Busang gold find if Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd and Barrick Gold Corp fail to meet a February deadline.

"Surely yes," he told reporters on Thursday night when asked if the government would look for other investors if Bre-X and Barrick failed to settle with local partners within the one- month given by his ministry from January 17.

Sudjana also did not dismiss the possibility of Placer Dome of Canada being involved in the development of the find, estimated by Bre-X to contain at least 57 million ounces of gold worth over $21 billion at current prices.
"There is a possibility," he said when asked if Placer could be involved in developing the property.
Placer has proposed a $5 billion merger with Bre-X and offered up to 40 percent of the property to Indonesian interests, including the government.

Indonesian mining officials had earlier raised concerns over Placer's environmental credentials because of its involvement in the Marcopper copper mine in the Philippines, which suffered a major tailings leak in March, 1996 polluting a local river.
Placer wrote off its investment in Marcopper last year and took a $43 million charge to earnings for the accident.
The Mines and Energy Ministry wrote to Bre-X and Barrick on January 17 telling them to settle with their local partners within one month or everything discussed previously would be cancelled.
A ministry official told Reuters on Thursday that if the companies failed to meet the deadline, the government was prepared to take control of the property.
He said an explicit warning to this effect had been contained in a letter to be sent to the companies on January 17, but had been deleted before actual dispatch because it was "too strong".
When asked if PT Askatindo Karya Minerals, which has a 10 percent stake in Busang II and III -- the richest parts of the find in partnership with Bre-X -- would get a bigger stake, Sudjana said:
"It depends on them. The government will leave it to them. They will report the results of their negotiations to the government. Let's see the development."
Indonesian timber baron Muhammad "Bob" Hassan, a close associate of President Suharto, was reported last week to have bought into Askatindo.
Sudjana also confirmed the deadline given to Bre-X and Barrick, saying he had sent the letter to them on January 17.
Bre-X and Barrick made a submission to the government last month outlining their agreement to jointly develop the find.
The submission from the Canadian firms said Bre-X would take a 22.5 percent stake in the Busang property and Barrick 67.5 percent. The government would own the remaining 10 percent.
Clouding the picture is a C$2.0 billion (US$1.48 billion) lawsuit filed in Canada last week by Indonesian businessman Jusuf Merukh, who claims 40 percent of the Busang find.
Merukh has a 10 percent interest in the Busang I area, which has the poorest potential for gold extraction from all of the three adjoining Busang areas.

Bre-X last October announced a deal with PT Panutan Duta, controlled by Suharto's eldest son, Sigit Harjojudanto, while Barrick is involved with the Citra Group, controlled by Suharto's eldest daughter Siti Hardiyanti Rukmana.
